review_notes: I read the whole file. I checked its simp interface: `mem_sInter`, `mem_sUnion`, `mem_iUnion`, `mem_iInter`, and the four `*_eq_*` lemmas (`sSup_eq_sUnion`, `sInf_eq_sInter`, `iSup_eq_iUnion`, `iInf_eq_iInter`). The four `*_eq_*` lemmas are `rfl` simp lemmas. They rewrite the generic order operations on `Set α` into the set-specific constants, which is a consistent normal form. None of them rewrites back, so I found no cycle. I looked at Mathlib uses (for example in `Order/LiminfLimsup.lean`, `MeasureTheory/SetSemiring.lean` and `MeasureTheory/Measure/AddContent.lean`). They rely on exactly this orientation and use the reverse direction only through explicit `←`. The membership lemmas have the expected unfolded forms. The indexed double-binder versions (`mem_iUnion₂`, `mem_iInter₂`) are not simp lemmas, but they are redundant, because `simp_rw [mem_iUnion]` already reduces them, as their own proofs show. One small inconsistency remains: `mem_sInter` and `mem_sUnion` carry `grind =`, while `mem_iUnion` and `mem_iInter` do not. Downstream code compensates with explicit `grind [Set.mem_iUnion]`. That is a `grind` matter rather than a simp-interface defect, so I did not report it. I did not search for competing simp lemmas in other files beyond a few greps, so some uncertainty remains. I found no justified simp-interface finding.
